notes:
Adversary run by Lab (for Rusty) against the UNMODIFIED v1.1.3 CommitEngine. I hold three genuine determinations (ISSUED authorize motto; REFUSED refuse set_maturity=mature; EXPIRED authorize tone) but not the private key, and keys are fresh per run so no signature can be forged offline.

RESULT I EXPECT THE HARNESS TO CONFIRM: TARGET GREEN. The only ACCEPTs are the single honest use of ISSUED (which sets personality.motto only) and the same honest auth carrying a misleading free-text reason; maturity never leaves juvenile, no organ installs, policy is unchanged, history verifies, and ISSUED never commits twice. Everything else REFUSES or is caught as ADAPTER_REFUSE, plus a cluster of FAULTs described below.

WHY THE DOOR HOLDS ON THIS CHANNEL: authorization is an Ed25519 signature over a canonical body that pins organism_id, trace/proposal/predecessor/resulting digests, policy+maturity, mutation_type, nonce and expiry. The engine re-derives every one of those from the submitted proposal/trace and from its own current state, so editing any field invalidates the signature, and reusing a real signature over a different transition fails the binding/verify. decision must be AUTHORIZE, predecessor must equal the live state digest, nonce+determination_id are consumed once, expiry is inside the signed body. The generic 'set' op is fenced to the personality root with an NFKC-casefold + recursive scan that blocks maturity/organs and their Unicode aliases; maturity and organs have dedicated ops; restore_state only accepts a digest already in history; install_organ needs artifact bytes whose sha256 matches a signed digest. No single signature I hold authorizes a policy-violating transition, so M6/M12-style weaknesses are unreachable from data alone.

FAULT FINDINGS (harness-reproduced; fail closed = no commit, but raise a bare exception instead of Refusal, so a caller that catches only Refusal/PermissionError would crash - a denial-of-service / robustness gap, not an authorization bypass):
  F1 non-string evidence_id (list or dict) -> TypeError 'unhashable type' in TraceValidator.validate_proposal, BEFORE the signature check (matches the baseline's documented FAULT). Also reachable via list-valued detector, maturity_state, etc.
  F2 non-string signature (int/list) -> bytes.fromhex() TypeError in MinatoAuthority.verify.
  F3 non-int trace.created_at (string) -> unorderable '<' TypeError in validate_trace.
  F4 huge-integer confidence (e.g. 1e400 written as a 400-digit int) -> OverflowError converting to float in the [0,1] range check.
  F5 1e400 as a float literal slips past strict_loads's parse_constant guard (which only rejects the NaN/Infinity KEYWORDS) and decodes to inf; the first canonical_json over it raises ValueError 'Out of range float values'. The strict loader is not actually infinity-proof.
  F6 a lone UTF-16 surrogate (\ud800) in any field that reaches canonical_json (e.g. reason on an otherwise-valid commit) -> UnicodeEncodeError, because canonical_json uses ensure_ascii=False. This one can abort a commit AT the persist/record step.
  F7 (separate, harness-level, not in an attempt): deeply nested JSON (~1000+) makes the harness's own recursive resolve()/strict_loads crash with an uncaught RecursionError before the engine runs. Harness robustness, not the door.
SUGGESTED FIXES: type-check evidence_id/detector/maturity_state/signature as non-empty str and created_at as int at the validation boundary; bound-check numeric fields as finite floats in [0,1] before float() conversion; reject non-finite/out-of-range numbers in strict_loads by post-validating parsed floats, not just the keyword constants; and wrap canonical_json so a surrogate/serialization error becomes a Refusal. None of these are breaches; the authorization core held against every transition I could express.

KILL SCORE: this corpus is built to kill the same M1/M2/M4 the baseline kills (forged-but-fully-bound authorize envelope; genuine REFUSE used as-is; genuine EXPIRED used as-is). The documented survivors (M3 replay double-guarded; M5/M8/M9 signer/constructor seams; M6/M12 need a signature over a policy-violating transition; M7 BOM path; M10/M11 need in-process object injection) are not reachable from a data-only JSON channel, so they survive as designed.
